bug_semantics: A malicious Nomad task that can modify its allocation logs directory can replace a stdout or stderr FIFO, or the logs directory itself, with a symlink. On task restart, the host-side logmon process follows that symlink as the Nomad process user: a substituted FIFO can make logmon read a host file into attacker-readable task logs, while a substituted logs directory can make logmon create partially attacker-named FIFOs or log files in a host directory. The fix confines FIFO operations with os.Root and mkfifoat and mounts the allocation logs subdirectory read-only for filesystem-isolated tasks.
flaw_origin: Public PR #4656 member dd220bfb36a03668102c9c727a5c97c638056a67 first added the host-side logmon plugin and its unchecked fifo.New(path) reader in client/logmon/logmon.go. Its immediate parent 6ab891313bb01f69a19411bda4d1625de3bbc447 has no client/logmon tree. The member was later represented in main by the single-parent aggregate 5b14d24bf4626bab420d00783d92bcf25e0b641e (executor v2, #4656), which entered v0.9.0 but not v0.8.6.
ai_marker: No AI-generation marker is present on the BIC. The public member is authored and committed by Nick Ethier <nethier@hashicorp.com>; its message is 'logmon: new logmon plugin to manage task logs' with no AI or co-author trailer. The only generated-code notice in the diff is protoc-gen-go's conventional generated protobuf header, not an AI marker.
evidence: The HashiCorp HCSEC-2026-14 bulletin and the PUBLISHED CVE-2026-6959 CNA record identify affected Nomad versions from 0.9.0 below 2.0.1 and fixed releases 2.0.1, 1.11.5, and 1.10.11; GitHub maps GHSA-3934-423w-4jq3 to the same CVE and fix.

Commit 2a09fd62c23880ff306499ae03fe64628d82a23f has sole parent 7939e3af3f36eb96278a5f96186462545c2887c0 and directly changes the FIFO opens to os.Root-relative no-follow operations, adds mkfifoat, and bind-mounts alloc/logs read-only. Its message describes both the host-file-read FIFO swap and logs-directory write primitive.

PR #4656 exposes 35 pre-aggregate member commits. Member dd220bfb36a03668102c9c727a5c97c638056a67 adds client/logmon/logmon.go and passes an allocation-controlled log-directory path to fifo.New; parent 6ab891313bb01f69a19411bda4d1625de3bbc447 has no client/logmon path. The main-history aggregate is 5b14d24bf4626bab420d00783d92bcf25e0b641e.

Local tag topology shows v0.8.6 at fcc4149c55399eb4979cd3fe3fb983cfe6c8449a does not contain aggregate 5b14d24bf4626bab420d00783d92bcf25e0b641e, while v0.9.0 at 28e768721992df5097203eea6e2b247abd56ca6f does, matching the vendor's lower affected boundary.

The v2.0.1 tag resolves to 5c11f948ba7e9e709abf7f2ab7895ba5b44feb39 and contains equivalent security backport 62bf44e1b1d2ccb9bf10c1338d803512f9dbd1d2; the main direct fix and backport have identical patch content. The vendor bulletin supplies the Enterprise 1.11.5 and 1.10.11 fixed boundaries.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and published, so FALSE_POSITIVE does not apply. The earliest reconstructable public first-write is the PR member that created host-side logmon with unchecked pathname-based FIFO opening; its parent lacks that component, and the later main commit is an aggregate rather than the atomic BIC. The direct fix reverses the relevant behavior by preventing symlink traversal and task writes to the logs directory. Attribution is based only on the BIC: it has conventional human authorship and no AI-generation signal, so this is NOT_AI.
